scope: Proposition 5.1 (Positive-time Gaussian subsequential limits) of the manuscript “Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Universality-of-critical-quench-autocorrelations-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-October-5-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12d511db42d09b8c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every sequence of Gaussian system sizes tending to infinity has a further represented subsequence on which the following assertions hold almost surely. The edge coordinates converge to g, and there is a measurable random family hs ∈ L2(Πg), s > 0, with the following properties. The family may at this stage depend on the represented data in addition to g. There is a finite random C ≥ 1, independent of s, t, such that 0 ≤ hs ≤ K(s) := C exp(Cs−77/50 ), Πg[hs] = 1, hs+t = Sg t hs, s, t > 0, (5.1) where Sg t = exp(−tc∗Hg). The map s 7→ hs is continuous in L2(Πg). For each t > 0, Sg t has a nonnegative symmetric kernel kg t relative to Πg satisfying 0 ≤ kg t (x, y) ≤ K(t) for Πg ⊗ Πg-almost every (x, y). (5.2) The constant 77/50 is the exponent 1.54 in Theorem 4.1. On this subsequence, An,J −→ Ag in Cloc((0, ∞)), Bn,J −→ Bh in Cloc((0, ∞)2 ), (5.3) where Bh(s, t) = X a≥1 Πg[hsxa Sg t xa]. (5.4) The series in (5.4) converges locally uniformly and is continuous. Finally, ∥hs − 1∥L2(Πg) −→ 0, Bh(s, ·) −→ Ag(·) in Cloc((0, ∞)) (s → ∞). (5.5)
